paper_title: Gated Attention for Large Language Models Non-linearity, Sparsity, and   Attention-Sink-Free
caption: Comparison of massive activations and attention sink phenomena across different gating configurations. Row 1 (Baseline): Significant massive activations and attention sinks emerge after the 6th layer. Row 2 (SDPA Gating): Reduced activations and no attention sinks observed. Row 3 (Value Layer Gating): Similar activations to Row 2 but with residual attention sinks. Rows 4–5 (Reduced Sparsity via cross-head share and NS-sigmoid): Massive activations and attention sinks resemble the baseline.

model_annotations.Bulgarian:
The provided figure illustrates the variation of the first token attention score across layers in a model with an attention output gate, as indicated by the title "first token attention score of atten_output_gate_head_share". It plots a single data series against the layer index, with a horizontal line indicating the mean value.

The horizontal axis (X-axis) is labeled "layer" and uses a linear scale ranging from 0 to 20. The tick marks are placed at integer intervals, with labeled values at 0, 5, 10, 15, and 20. The vertical axis (Y-axis) is labeled "first token attention score" and also uses a linear scale, ranging from 0.0 to 1.0. The tick marks are placed at intervals of 0.2, with labeled values at 0.0, 0.2, 0.4, 0.6, and 0.8.

A single blue line, marked with solid circles, represents the "first token attention score". This line begins at approximately 0.02 at layer 0, dips to a low of approximately 0.01 at layer 1, rises to a peak of approximately 0.58 at layer 6, then fluctuates between approximately 0.30 and 0.50 until layer 15. It peaks again at approximately 0.60 at layer 16, then declines sharply to approximately 0.05 at layer 20, before ending at approximately 0.02 at layer 20. A horizontal dashed green line is drawn at the value 0.301, labeled "mean: 0.301", which remains constant across the entire range of the X-axis.
